bottlenecks.reading: Advanced packaging (CoWoS) is the tightest AI bottleneck: a supply-demand gap of ~20% reportedly narrowing to ~10% by end-2026; TSMC reportedly plans to roughly double capacity by 2028 and seeks ~20% CoWoS price rises. Analyst/press estimates, not TSMC guidance.

Leading-edge wafers are concentrated: TSMC held 72.5% of 2Q26 foundry revenue (Samsung 5.9%, SMIC 5.4%); 20-F says 3/5/7nm were 24%/36%/14% of 2025 wafer revenue (74% advanced). No rival has yet shown external volume at comparable nodes.
Pricing power signal: wafer prices reportedly rising 3-6% from Jan 2027 with 2nm/3nm steepest (press report of TrendForce, unconfirmed by TSMC).

Share risk hypothesis: Intel 18A/14A could win some external AI/PC volume from 2H26-2028 (Tesla 14A reported; Apple reports are analyst claims). Intel external foundry revenue is only $293M in 2Q26 vs TSMC ~$40.2B.

notes: fd NAMED COMPETITORS (20-F Item 1/1A, pf_10k_20260416): the 20-F names no competitor companies; it says TSMC competes with 'other foundry service providers' and 'integrated device manufacturers', some with government subsidies (US/China/EU/Korea/Japan). Names in competitors[] are our identification, not TSMC's.

fd SHARE 2Q26 foundry revenue share (TrendForce): TSMC 72.5% (1Q26 72.3%), Samsung 5.9% (6.5%), SMIC 5.4% (5.1%), UMC 3.9%; top-10 revenue $53.49B, TSMC ~$40.2B +12.1% QoQ. Sources fd_trendforce_2q26, fd_evertiq_2q26. Counterpoint (pure foundry, different basis) shows TSMC ~73%, GlobalFoundries 4%: fd_counterpoint_2q26.

fd SHARE trajectory: TSMC edging up (+0.2pt QoQ), Samsung losing (-0.6pt), SMIC gaining (+0.3pt, domestic substitution, hypothesis on cause). Only two quarters of share data read; no multi-year series.
fd SHARE Intel: 2025 revenue -0.5%, operating margin -4.2% (pf_peer_INTC); external foundry revenue $293M in 2Q26 (fd_intel_q2_2026), i.e. under 1% of TSMC's quarter.
